title: Chapter 2: Biological Molecules
content:
❤️ ውድና የተወደዳችሁ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን — እንኳን በሰላም መጣችሁ!

ውድ እህቶቻችንና ወንድሞቻችን፣ የነገ የሀገራችን ተስፋዎች! 🌟 በቅድሚያ በታላቅ አክብሮትና በልብ በሞላ የቤተሰባዊ ፍቅር እንኳን ወደዚህ Biology Chapter 2: Biological Molecules (Macromolecules) ሁለተኛ ክፍል የፈተና ዝግጅት ኖት በሰላም መጣችሁልን! ❤️ የአንደኛ ዓመት የዩኒቨርሲቲ ህይወት አዲስ አካባቢ፣ አዲስ የትምህርት ስልትና ሰፊ ሞጁሎችን የያዘ በመሆኑ መጀመሪያ ላይ ትንሽ ከበድ ብሎ ሊታያችሁ እንደሚችል እንረዳለን። ነገር ግን በፍጹም አትጨነቁ! እናንተ ብቻችሁን አይደላችሁም፤ እኛ ሁልጊዜም ከጎናችሁ አለን። ተከታተሉን!

2.3. Proteins (ፕሮቲኖች)

Self Test Questions :
1. Comment on the following statements (True/False & Elaborate):
    a) All proteins are enzymes: FALSE. While all enzymes are proteins (except catalytic RNA/ribozymes), NOT all proteins are enzymes. Proteins have many non-enzymatic roles such as structural support (collagen, keratin), transport (hemoglobin), and defense (antibodies).
    b) Enzymes initiate a chemical reaction: FALSE. Enzymes do NOT initiate or cause a reaction that wouldn't otherwise occur. Instead, they speed up (catalyze) thermodynamically feasible reactions by lowering the activation energy.
    c) Chemical reactions cannot take place in the body without enzymes: ELABORATION: Chemical reactions CAN technically occur without enzymes, but at an extremely slow rate that is insufficient to sustain life. Enzymes accelerate these reactions millions of times.
2. Elemental composition of proteins: Carbon (C), Nitrogen (N), Oxygen (O), Hydrogen (H), and sometimes Sulfur (S).
3. Physiological and structural roles: Structural support (muscles, skin, hair), cellular transport, signal communication inside/between cells, enzyme catalysis, and controlling cell growth.
4. Compare protein with nucleic acid: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds (composed of C, H, O, N, S) that function in structure, catalysis, and transport. Nucleic acids are polymers of nucleotides linked by phosphodiester bonds (composed of C, H, O, N, P) that store and transmit genetic information.
5. How is the primary structure of a protein determined? Determined by the sequence and exact number of amino acids joined in a polypeptide chain, as specified by the genetic code/DNA sequence.

A protein is a complex biological compound made of small organic monomers called amino acids. Amino acids consist of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, hydrogen, and sometimes sulfur atoms. All standard amino acids share a central (alpha) carbon atom bonded to four distinct covalent chemical groups:

  1. A Hydrogen atom (-H)
  2. An Amino group (-NH₂) - basic functional group
  3. A Carboxyl group (-COOH) - acidic functional group
  4. A Variable side chain (-R group) - confers unique chemical properties to each amino acid
The variable group (-R) is what distinguishes one amino acid from another. Because there are 20 different variable groups, there are 20 standard amino acids that combine in various sequences to construct thousands of proteins.

          R (Variable side chain)
          |
H₂N — C — C(=O)OH
(Amino) | (Carboxyl)
          H (Hydrogen atom)

Fig: 2.3. Basic structure of amino acid

Peptide Bond Formation:
Amino acids are linked together by covalent bonds called peptide bonds. A peptide bond forms between the amino group (-NH₂) of one amino acid and the carboxyl group (-COOH) of another amino acid. Two joined amino acids form a dipeptide, while a long chain forms a polypeptide.

H     R₁     H     R₂
\    |      |     |
 N — C — C — N — C — C — OH
/    |      ||    |     ||
H     H      O     H     O
             ↑ Peptide bond
             Dipeptide

Fig: 2.4. Peptide bond

Levels of Protein Structure:
Proteins can exhibit up to four hierarchical levels of structure:

  • 1. Primary Structure: The linear sequence and exact number of amino acids in a chain.
  • 2. Secondary Structure: Local folding, helices, pleats, and folds in the polypeptide chain.
  • 3. Tertiary Structure: The overall 3D shape of a single protein chain. Can be globular (e.g., Hemoglobin, enzymes) or fibrous (e.g., Collagen, Keratin).
  • 4. Quaternary Structure: Spatial arrangement formed when two or more polypeptide chains combine to form a functional complex.
Proteins make up about 15% of total body mass. A single cell contains about 10,000 different proteins performing structural support, transport, signal communication, catalysis, and cell growth control.

ፕሮቲኖች የሰውነታችን ዋና ግንባታ ክፍሎች ናቸው። የተሰሩት ከ Amino acids ሲሆን፣ በውስጣቸው Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, Hydrogen እና አንዳንዴ Sulfur ይይዛሉ። እያንዳንዱ Amino acid 4 ነገሮችን በማዕከላዊ Carbon ላይ ይዟል፡ Hydrogen atom፣ Amino group (-NH₂)፣ Carboxyl group (-COOH)፣ እና Variable group (-R)። የ -R group አይነት ለ 20ውም Amino acids ይለያያል። አሚኖ አሲዶች እርስ በርሳቸው የሚያያዙት Peptide bond በተባለ ጠንካራ covalent bond ነው (በ Carboxyl እና Amino group መካከል በሚፈጠር ትስስር)። ፕሮቲኖች 4 አይነት መዋቅር (Structure) አሏቸው፡ Primary (የአሚኖ አሲዶች ቅደም ተከተል)፣ Secondary (Helices, Pleats እና Folds)፣ Tertiary (3D ቅርፅ/Globular or Fibrous)፣ እና Quaternary (ብዙ የፖሊፔፕታይድ ሰንሰለቶች ሲጣመሩ)። በሰውነታችን ውስጥ ከ 10,000 በላይ የተለዩ ፕሮቲኖች አሉ።

ተብሎ ከተጠየቀ መልሱ Primary Structure ነው። እንዲሁም

የፕሮቲን Primary Structure እና የFreshman ተማሪ የዶርም ዕቃ ሰልፍ አንድ ናቸው — አንዱ ቦታ ከተቀየረ አጠቃላይ መዋቅሩ ተበላሸ ማለት ነው! 😅 አሚኖ አሲዶቹ ቦታቸውን እንደጠበቁ ሁሉ እናንተም የጥናት ሰሌዳችሁን ጠብቁ!

2.4. Nucleic Acids (ኑክሊክ አሲዶች) & ATP

Self Test Questions :
1. What is the role of nucleic acid? To store and transmit genetic information inside living organisms.
2. What are the molecular composition of nucleotides? Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, Phosphorus, and Hydrogen atoms forming a Phosphate group, a 5-carbon pentose sugar (ribose/deoxyribose), and a Nitrogenous base.
3. Describe briefly the differences between DNA & RNA: DNA is double-stranded, contains deoxyribose sugar and Thymine; RNA is single-stranded, contains ribose sugar and Uracil.

Nucleic acids are complex biological macromolecules that store and transmit genetic information. They are polymers composed of repeating monomer subunits called nucleotides.

Structure of a Nucleotide:
Each nucleotide monomer consists of three covalently bonded chemical units:

  1. Phosphate Group
  2. Pentose Sugar (5-Carbon Sugar): Ribose or Deoxyribose
  3. Nitrogenous Base: Divided into two structural families:
    • Purine Bases (Double-ring structure): Adenine (A) and Guanine (G).
    • Pyrimidine Bases (Single-ring structure): Cytosine (C), Thymine (T - DNA only), and Uracil (U - RNA only).
Nucleotides link together as the sugar of one nucleotide bonds to the phosphate group of another nucleotide, forming a continuous chain.

[ Phosphate Group ] — [ Pentose Sugar ] — [ Nitrogenous Base ]

Fig: 2.5. Basic structure of nucleotide

Purine Bases (Double-ring) Pyrimidine Bases (Single-ring)
• Adenine (A)
• Guanine (G)		 • Cytosine (C)
• Thymine (T - DNA only)
• Uracil (U - RNA only)

Fig: 2.6. Nitrogenous bases

Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP):
ATP is a specialized nucleotide containing an Adenine base, a Ribose sugar, and three phosphate groups. It acts as the storehouse of chemical energy in cells. Energy is released when the high-energy bond between the second and third phosphate group is broken (hydrolyzed).

Comparison Table: DNA vs. RNA

Feature DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) RNA (Ribonucleic Acid)
Strand Structure Double-stranded helix Single-stranded chain
Sugar Component Deoxyribose sugar Ribose sugar
Nitrogenous Bases Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, Thymine Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, Uracil
Primary Function Long-term genetic information storage Protein synthesis and gene expression

👉
ኑክሊክ አሲዶች የዘረመል (Genetic) መረጃዎችን የሚያስቀምጡ እና የሚያስተላልፉ ግዙፍ ሞለኪውሎች ናቸው። የተሰሩት Nucleotides ከተባሉ አነስተኛ ክፍሎች ነው። አንድ Nucleotide 3 ነገሮችን ይዟል፡ Phosphate group, 5-Carbon Sugar (Ribose/Deoxyribose) እና Nitrogenous Base። Nitrogenous base-ዎች በሁለት ይከፈላሉ፡ Purines (ሁለት ቀለበት/Double ring አላቸው፡ Adenine እና Guanine) እና Pyrimidines (አንድ ቀለበት/Single ring አላቸው፡ Cytosine, Thymine, Uracil)። Thymine የሚገኘው በ DNA ብቻ ሲሆን Uracil ደግሞ በ RNA ብቻ ነው የሚገኘው። ATP ደግሞ 3 Phosphate ያለው ልዩ Nucleotide ሲሆን ለሴሎቻችን የሃይል ምንጭ (Energy currency) ነው፤ በ 2ኛው እና በ 3ኛው Phosphate መካከል ያለው ቦንድ ሲሰበር ሀይል ይለቀቃል።

ተብሎ አዘውትሮ ይጠየቃል። መልሱ Uracil (U) ነው! እንዲሁም

ከተባለ መልሱ Adenine (A) and Guanine (G) ነው።

ATP በሴላችን ውስጥ እንደ ቴሌግራም ካርድ ነው! ባላንስ ሲኖረው ሴሉ ይሰራል፣ ሲያልቅ ደግሞ ሴሉ 'Low Battery' ብሎ ስራ ያቆማል! ATP-አችሁን አትጨርሱ 😅!

2.5. Vitamins (ቪታሚኖች)

Self Test Questions :
1. What are vitamins? Organic compounds required in small amounts for normal metabolic activities.
2. What are the roles of vitamins in maintaining homeostasis? They assist enzymes to function properly (coenzymes) and regulate metabolic biological processes.
3. What are the water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins? Fat-soluble: Vitamins A, D, E, K. Water-soluble: Vitamin B complex and Vitamin C.

Vitamins are essential organic compounds needed in small amounts for metabolic activities. Many vitamins directly help enzymes function well in the body.

Sources & Synthesis of Specific Vitamins:

  • Vitamin D: Made directly by cells in human skin upon exposure to sunlight.
  • Vitamin B Complex and Vitamin K: Produced by beneficial bacteria living inside the large intestine.
  • Dietary Ingestion: Sufficient quantities of most other vitamins cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be regularly supplied through a well-balanced diet.

Classification of Vitamins:

Category Vitamins Included Storage & Excretion Characteristics
Fat-Soluble Vitamins Vitamin A, D, E, K Stored in small quantities in the liver and fatty tissues of the body.
Water-Soluble Vitamins Vitamin B complex, Vitamin C Cannot be stored in the body; excess is excreted. Foods providing adequate levels must be included in regular diet.

👉
ቪታሚኖች በሰውነታችን ውስጥ በትንሽ መጠን (Micro-amount) የሚፈልጉ ኦርጋኒክ ውህዶች ናቸው። ዋና ስራቸው ኢንዛይሞች ስራቸውን በአግባቡ እንዲሰሩ መርዳት ነው። Vitamin D በቆዳችን ሴሎች አማካኝነት ይሰራል። Vitamin B እና Vitamin K ደግሞ በትልቁ አንጀት (Large intestine) ውስጥ በሚኖሩ ጠቃሚ ባክቴሪያዎች ይመረታሉ። ቪታሚኖች በሁለት ይከፈላሉ፡ Fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) - በስብ ውስጥ የሚሟሙና በጉበት/Fat tissue የሚቀመጡ፤ እና Water-soluble (B complex, C) - በውሃ ውስጥ የሚሟሙና በሰውነት ውስጥ ስለማይከማቹ በየቀኑ በምግብ ውስጥ መወሰድ ያለባቸው ናቸው።

💡 Exam Hint:
ተብሎ ቢጠየቅ መልሱ Vitamin B and Vitamin K ነው።

ከተባለ መልሱ Water-soluble vitamins (B and C) ነው።

Water-soluble vitamins በሰውነታችን ውስጥ መቀመጥ አይወዱም! 'አልቆይም' ብለው በሽንት ወጥተው ይሄዳሉ። ስለዚህ በየቀኑ ፍራፍሬ አትተው! 🍊😅

2.6. Water (ውሃ)

Self Test Questions :
What are the physical and chemical properties of water, and their roles in maintaining homeostasis? Water molecules are formed by covalent bonds linking 2 hydrogen atoms to 1 oxygen atom. Water is odorless, tasteless, exists in solid, liquid, and gas states, has high solvent capabilities for dissolving and transporting substances, and consists of polar molecules with unequal charge distributions that help maintain homeostasis.

Water (H₂O) is one of the most plentiful and essential compounds in living organisms. A water molecule is formed by covalent bonds linking two hydrogen (H) atoms to one oxygen (O) atom.

Polarity & Solvent Capabilities of Water:
Water molecules have an unequal distribution of electrical charges, making them polar molecules with oppositely charged regions. This versatility as a solvent allows water to dissolve and act as a media for transporting many substances throughout living organisms.

Activity (Think Scientifically) Solutions:
1. What would have happened to living things if the color of water was black or red?
If water were dark/colored, sunlight could not penetrate aquatic bodies. Photosynthetic aquatic organisms could not perform photosynthesis, causing aquatic food chains and ecosystems to collapse.
2. Mystery behind water supporting life on Earth vs. other planets:
Water exists in a stable liquid state within Earth's temperature and atmospheric conditions, enabling essential biochemical reactions and physiological transport processes to occur.

👉
ውሃ በሁለት Hydrogen እና በአንድ Oxygen አተሞች በ Covalent bond የተሰራ ውህድ ነው። Water molecules ኤሌክትሮኖችን እኩል ባለማካፈላቸው Polar molecules ይባላሉ (ተቃራኒ ቻርጅ ያላቸው ክፍሎች አሏቸው)። ይህም ውሃ ሁለገብ கரைች (Solvent) እንዲሆንና ንጥረ ነገሮች የሚጓጓዙበት ዋና (Transport medium) እንዲሆን ያስችለዋል።

2.7. Minerals (ሚኔራሎች)

Self Test Questions :
1. What are minerals? Inorganic compounds used by the body as building materials and involved with metabolic functions.
2. What are the roles of minerals in maintaining homeostasis? They build structural tissues (bones/teeth), regulate muscle and nerve functions, transport oxygen, and act as cofactors for enzymes.

Minerals are inorganic compounds used by living organisms as structural building materials and vital metabolic regulators.

Key Minerals Featured in the Module:

Mineral Biological Role & Location Key Function
Iron (Fe) Red blood cells Needed to make hemoglobin; binds oxygen in red blood cells to deliver it to body cells.
Calcium (Ca) Bones, muscles, nerves Important component of bones; involved in muscle and nerve functions, and acts as cofactor for enzymes.
Magnesium (Mg) Plant chloroplasts Important central component of the green pigment chlorophyll, involved in photosynthesis.

Activity Solution:
Explain why raw edible oil is added on dishes of raw vegetables before consumption?
Answer: Raw vegetables contain essential fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K). Adding raw edible oil (a lipid solvent) allows these fat-soluble vitamins to dissolve in the oil, promoting efficient absorption in the digestive tract!

👉
ሚኔራሎች በሰውነታችን ውስጥ አካልን ለመገንባትና የሜታቦሊዝም ስራዎችን ለማከናወን የሚያስፈልጉ Inorganic (ኢ-ኦርጋኒክ) ውህዶች ናቸው።
1. Iron (ብረት): በደማችን የቀይ ደም ህዋሳት ውስጥ የ Hemoglobin ዋና አካል ሲሆን ኦክሲጅንን ለመሸከም ያገለግላል።
2. Calcium (ካልሲየም): የአጥንታችን ዋና አካል ነው፤ ለጡንቻና ለነርቭ ስራዎች እንዲሁም ለኢንዛይሞች እንደ Cofactor ያገለግላል።
3. Magnesium (ማግኒዚየም): በእፅዋት ውስጥ የ Chlorophyll አረንጓዴ ፒግመንት አካል ሲሆን ለ Photosynthesis ወሳኝ ነው!

💡 Exam Hint:
ፈተና ላይ የሚከተሉትን ጥንዶች በደንብ ያዙ፡
- Iron → Hemoglobin (Oxygen transport)
- Magnesium → Chlorophyll (Photosynthesis)
- Calcium → Bones & Enzyme Cofactor

📌 Summary of Unit Two

  • Carbon compounds are the basic building blocks of living organisms.
  • Biological macromolecules are formed by joining of small carbon compounds into polymers.
  • There are four types of biological macromolecules: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.
  • Monosaccharides undergo condensation to form disaccharides and polysaccharides through glycosidic linkages.
  • Peptide bonds join amino acids in proteins.
  • Lipids are esters of fatty acids and alcohols.
  • Chains of nucleotides form nucleic acids.
